key_insight: Clinician review removed most unsupported additions from AI-drafted paediatric discharge documents but missed most incorrect abbreviation expansions.
clinical_relevance: AI-assisted drafting used more common vocabulary in family documents without a detectable improvement in record-concordant understanding at follow-up.
method: Randomised 153 paediatric emergency department discharges to conventional templates or an on-premises open-weight LLM.
Discharging clinicians validated documents in both arms; 117 cases were analysed.
Exploratory comparisons tracked errors from source records through drafts to delivered documents.
evidence_signal: Reviewers removed 18/22 unsupported additions but only 6/22 incorrect abbreviation expansions; the primary understanding outcome differed by -0.01 (95% CI -0.12 to 0.10), and no delivered physician-facing discrepancy was judged seriously consequential (0/117).
watch_item: Exploratory error counts and a small analysed sample limit safety conclusions; edit frequency alone cannot establish effective oversight.
paper_title: From clinician review to measurable human oversight of AI-drafted paediatric discharge documents
